## Four major service guarantees

|  |
| --- |
| System availability and support periods are based on product versions, deployment programmes and service level agreements. |

### System stability and service levels

|  |
| --- |
| Disaster response structures and failure transfer capabilities are based on product versions and deployment programmes. |
| Load equilibrium and elasticity are dependent on product version, deployment resources and configuration. |
| Monitoring, early warning and trouble management mechanisms are based on deployment programmes and service level agreements. |

### Data security and compliance security

|  |
| --- |
| Encrypted transmission, storage and permission controls are supported; the specific algorithm, scope and configuration are based on the corresponding product information. |
| Supporting hierarchical access controls to reduce the risk of over-authorization. |
| The data backup and recovery strategy depends on the product version, deployment modalities and contractual engagement. |

### Platform stability and continuous evolution

|  |
| --- |
| The release mechanism and operational impact depend on the product version, deployment architecture and change options. |
| The scope of the version compatibility and the impact of the upgrade need to be confirmed in the issuance of the notes and the upgrading programme. |
| The product iterative range is based on officially published plans and version descriptions. |

### Rapid technical support by profession

|  |
| --- |
| Support is available through worksheets, online passenger service and service lines; service hours and response levels are based on contracts or service-level agreements. |
| Technical support staff could be deployed under the service programme. |
| Whether the inspection, health check and optimization recommendations are included in the service is governed by the contract or service level agreement. |
